claims: Allah is the Arabic term for the one, supreme, and universal God in Islam.
Allah is the Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
Allah is worshipped directly without partners.
Allah is viewed as the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Judge of the universe.
Islam emphasizes that God is singular, without partner, child, or equal.
Allah is transcendent and beyond human comprehension.
Allah is considered closer to human beings than their own jugular vein.
"Allah" is derived from al-ilāh.
Al-ilāh means "the God".
"Allah" is used by Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews as well.
The Quran and Hadith refer to Allah with numerous attributes.
Allah's attributes are often summarized as the 99 Beautiful Names (al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā).
Ar-Raḥmān means The Most Merciful.
Ar-Raḥīm means The Bestower of Mercy.
Al-Khāliq means The Creator.
Al-Ḥakīm means The Wise.
Al-ʿAlīm means The All-Knowing.
Muslims believe Allah alone deserves worship.
Worship of Allah requires no mediators.
The core of Islamic faith is islām.
Islām means "surrender" or "submission" to the will of Allah.
Worship of Allah includes daily prayers (Salah).
Worship of Allah includes fasting during Ramadan.
Worship of Allah includes charity.
Worship of Allah includes pilgrimage.
Daily prayers (Salah), fasting during Ramadan, charity, and pilgrimage are instructed through the Prophet Muhammad in the Quran.
Allah is not a "Muslim god".
Allah is not an Arab moon god.
Allah is the same God worshipped by Christians and Jews, just referred to in Arabic.
The term Allah is neither feminine nor masculine.
The term Allah cannot be made plural.
